summary: iter 102 — verified new 'name from PAN/Aadhaar' + passport-wins rule end-to-end. Backend pytest (14/14): name_exact enforces STRICT same-words-same-order (case/space ignored) — e.g. 'Ravi Kumar Reddy' vs 'Ravi Reddy Kumar' → False, 'Ravi Kumar' vs 'Ravi Kumar Sharma' → False; POST /api/members/{mid}/id-docs/self/pan/use-name title-cases 'RAVI KUMAR' → 'Ravi Kumar'; aadhaar/use-name applies as printed and only collapses whitespace: '  Ravi   KUMAR ' → 'Ravi KUMAR'; parent field path works ('amit  SINGH' → father_name='amit SINGH'); empty-name → 400; non-athlete parent person → 400; audit action is 'name_from_aadhaar'. Passport-wins: after passport use-name sets name_from_passport=true, pan/aadhaar use-name return 409 with 'passport' in the error, passport use-name still allowed, lock is scoped per-person (father-locked doesn't block self); upload PAN after lock returns detected.name_locked=true. Bulk read /api/id-docs/bulk/read now exposes name_matches + name_locked for PAN/Aadhaar matches (not just passport). Masked aadhaar still returns number=null. All 18 regression tests in test_id_docs_and_tuition.py still pass (passport flow unchanged). Frontend Playwright on preview URL (admin login via toggle): (1) Uploaded synthetic Aadhaar PNG 'RAVI KUMAR REDDY' onto a throwaway member whose DB name was 'TEST Ravi Reddy <sfx>' — id-self-aadhaar-name-warning rendered with exact spec text 'Name is NOT exactly the same — Aadhaar: "RAVI KUMAR REDDY" · database: "TEST Ravi Reddy <sfx>"', id-self-aadhaar-use-name button labelled 'Use Aadhaar name'. Clicking it updated the DB full_name to 'RAVI KUMAR REDDY' (verified via /api/members) — case preserved, spacing kept, NO title-casing applied (correct per spec). (2) On a passport-locked member, same Aadhaar upload showed id-self-aadhaar-name-locked text 'The database name follows the passport (passport wins) — check this card instead.' and the Use Aadhaar name button was NOT rendered.

issues: Known from iter100: AbsentDispatchPrompt + Post-Leave-to-WhatsApp dialogs still appear on every fresh admin login. Playwright has to click 'Later' / dismiss testids before any member action. Also the browser routed admin@attendance.app initially to '/' (member Check-In view) and only after seeing the sidebar did /admin/members become usable — a networkidle wait on /admin/members times out because the preview sends several background pollers; use domcontentloaded + testid wait instead. Non-blocking.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/id_docs.py use_card_name: name = ' '.join(words if card == 'aadhaar' else (title) for w in words) correctly preserves aadhaar case and only collapses whitespace. The 409 'passport wins' guard runs BEFORE the users.update_one so a locked slot stays untouched. Audit action is parameterised 'name_from_{card}' — matches spec. One minor: the lock flag lives at people.{person}.name_from_passport inside member_id_docs, written by _lock_name via $set upsert — if a brand-new member_id_docs doc is created purely to hold name_from_passport, people.{person} is created as a bare {name_from_passport: True} dict. That's fine for the lock check, but downstream code that assumes a 'people.{person}' map always has number keys could be surprised. Current readers (_doc, report, bulk) all .get keys defensively, so OK.

upload_scan: detected.name_locked is False whenever card == 'passport' (short-circuit `card != 'passport' and await _name_locked(...)`). This matches spec — passport scans should never be greyed-out. Good.

frontend IdDocsSection.jsx: DetectedBar reads d.name_locked and renders either id-{p}-{card}-name-locked text or id-{p}-{card}-use-name button — matches backend contract. The applyCardName optimistically sets name_matches:true + expected_name:res.name after the API returns, so the warning disappears without a refetch. Nice.

frontend BulkIdUpload.jsx RowEditor similarly renders bulk-row-{key}-name-warning / -use-name / -name-locked. onUseName uses /{card}/use-name route — correct. One minor DRY: the warning + locked text copy differs between IdDocsSection and BulkIdUpload (bulk says 'Not exactly the database name' / 'Name follows the passport (passport wins)' vs the section's longer 'Name is NOT exactly the same —…'). Spec only pins the longer wording for the per-member section, so this is acceptable, but worth a comment linking the two.

services/id_ocr.py name_exact uses only _norm (upper + collapse spaces) and strict equality — exact same-words-same-order rule as spec. name_matches (used nowhere critical now) is still the old loose check; keep in mind if BulkIdUpload ever switches.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (2/2 scenarios: aadhaar warning→use-name applies as printed; passport-wins hides use-name button and shows name-locked text)

The passport-lock flag is `member_id_docs.people.{person}.name_from_passport = true`; set via POST /api/members/{mid}/id-docs/{person}/passport/use-name OR via upload_scan when an exact-match passport scan is accepted. Use-name endpoint is POST /api/members/{mid}/id-docs/{person}/{card}/use-name {name}; aadhaar keeps case + collapses whitespace; pan/passport Title Case. Tests use real Gemini (gemini-3.5-flash) — budget 15-30s per OCR; wait up to 90s for the UI warning after a file-input set.
